'''Armed conflicts and attacks'''
*[[Afghanistan conflict (1978–present)|Afghanistan conflict]]
**[[Kabul Airlift (2021)|Kabul Airlift]]
***A [[Qatar Airways]] charter flight carrying 200 passengers, including Afghans and [[Americans]], departs from [[Kabul International Airport]] to [[Qatar]]. [https://www.reuters.com/world/europe/qatar-flight-with-afghans-americans-europeans-leaves-kabul-official-says-2021-09-19/ (Reuters)]
**[[ISIL–Taliban conflict]]
***Three [[Taliban]] members and two civilians are killed when a bomb, planted by [[Islamic State of Iraq and the Levant – Khorasan Province|ISIL–K]], explodes near a Taliban vehicle in [[Jalalabad]], [[Nangarhar]]. [https://www.theguardian.com/world/2021/sep/18/three-killed-in-explosions-in-jalalabad-eastern-afghanistan (''The Guardian'')]
*[[Papua conflict]], [[Australia–Indonesia relations]]
**A recently declassified [[Australian Secret Intelligence Service|Australian intelligence]] report from 1998 reveals that the [[government of Australia|government]] was fully aware that the [[Indonesian military]] had [[massacre]]d peaceful protesters from the [[Free Papua Movement]], which was not publicly acknowledged or condemned by Australia at the time. ''[[Guardian Australia]]'' speculates that supporting photographic evidence may have been destroyed by [[Australian Government|Australian authorities]]. [https://www.theguardian.com/australia-news/2021/sep/19/killed-like-animals-documents-reveal-how-australia-turned-a-blind-eye-to-a-west-papuan-massacre (''The Guardian'')]
*[[Killamarsh murders]]
**Police officers have discovered the remains of three children and one adult inside a residential property in [[Killamarsh]], near [[Sheffield]], [[England]], after being called out to reports of a disturbance. A 31-year-old man has been arrested and a [[murder]] inquiry has been launched. [https://www.bbc.co.uk/news/uk-england-derbyshire-58622164 (BBC News)]

'''Arts and culture'''
*[[73rd Primetime Emmy Awards]]
**The 73rd annual [[Primetime Emmy Awards]] takes place at the [[L.A. Live|Event Deck]] in [[Los Angeles]], with ''[[Ted Lasso]]'' winning four Emmys. [[Brett Goldstein]], [[Jason Sudeikis]], and [[Hannah Waddingham]] win their first career Emmys. [https://deadline.com/2021/09/hannah-waddingham-wins-2021-emmy-supporting-actress-comedy-series-1234839032/ (Deadline)] [https://www.cnbc.com/2021/09/19/emmys-2021-live-blog-of-highlights-winners-from-the-73rd-emmy-awards.html (CNBC)]
*[[Impact of the COVID-19 pandemic on tourism]], [[Impact of the COVID-19 pandemic on the arts and cultural heritage]], [[COVID-19 pandemic in Iran]]
**[[Iran]] reopens museums in [[Tehran]] and other large cities with sanitary protocols after a year-long closure due to the pandemic. [https://www.rfi.fr/en/middle-east/20210919-iran-museums-reopen-after-year-long-covid-break (AFP via Radio France Internationale)]

'''Disasters and accidents'''
*[[2021 La Palma eruption]]
**The [[Cumbre Vieja]] volcano on the island of [[La Palma]], [[Canary Islands]], [[Spain]], erupts for the first time in fifty years. A few hours later, the first preventive evacuations of people with reduced mobility from nearby towns took place after the declaration of a state of pre-eruption. [https://www.reuters.com/world/europe/people-evacuated-spanish-island-la-palma-after-volcano-eruption-warning-2021-09-19/ (Reuters)] [https://www.eldiario.es/canariasahora/lapalmaahora/sociedad/nuevo-volcan-palma-estalla-montana-rajada_1_8316961.html (elDiario.es)]

'''Health and environment'''
*[[COVID-19 pandemic]]
**[[COVID-19 pandemic in Asia]]
***[[COVID-19 pandemic in Laos]]
****[[Laos|Laotian]] capital [[Vientiane]] enters in a strict lockdown for two weeks as the city reported a record number of COVID-19 cases. Travel between the hard-hit provinces is also banned and anyone wishing to enter the city must be quarantined for 14 days. [https://www.bangkokpost.com/world/2184815/laos-locks-down-capital-as-covid-cases-hit-record-high (Bangkok Post)] 
***[[COVID-19 pandemic in Malaysia]], [[COVID-19 vaccination in Malaysia]]
****The [[Malaysia]]n [[Government of Malaysia|government]] approves a plan to administer a [[COVID-19 vaccine]] [[booster dose]] for high-risk groups once the nationwide vaccination rate surpasses 80% of the adult population. [https://www.thestar.com.my/news/nation/2021/09/19/pm-frontliners-elderly-to-get-booster-shots-once-80-of-adults-vaccinated (''The Star'')]
***[[COVID-19 pandemic in Singapore]]
****[[Singapore]] reports 1,012 new cases of [[COVID-19]] in the past 24 hours, which is the highest single-day total of new cases since April 2020. [https://www.straitstimes.com/singapore/health/1012-new-covid-19-cases-in-spore-second-day-in-a-row-new-infections-cross-1000-mark (''The Straits Times'')]
***[[COVID-19 pandemic in the United Arab Emirates]], [[Travel restrictions related to the COVID-19 pandemic]]
****[[Emirate of Abu Dhabi|Abu Dhabi]] lifts the requirement for people from other [[Emirates of the United Arab Emirates|emirate]]s to receive [[COVID-19 testing]] before they enter the capital due to a decline in the number of COVID-19 cases. [https://www.thenationalnews.com/uae/transport/2021/09/18/abu-dhabi-to-remove-test-to-enter-requirement-from-tomorrow/ (''The National News'')]
*Sixty-three [[African penguin]]s are dead after being stung by a swarm of bees in [[Simon's Town]], [[South Africa]]. The African penguin is an endangered species. [https://www.bbc.com/news/world-africa-58622482 (BBC News)]

'''International relations'''
*[[Mexico–United States border crisis]]
**The [[United States]] closes the [[Mexico–United States border|Mexico–US border]] near the [[Texas]] city of [[Del Rio, Texas|Del Rio]] after thousands of Haitian migrants arrived at the [[Del Río–Ciudad Acuña International Bridge|International Bridge]] near the city. The U.S. will also begin flying the migrants back to [[Haiti]]. [https://apnews.com/article/immigration-border-haiti-mexico-texas-09d7de5bc57e1dbd92d40751c0d91f69 (AP)]

'''Law and crime'''
*[[Gilboa Prison break]]
**The [[Israel Defense Forces]] announces that all six [[Palestinian prisoners of Israel|Palestinian fugitives]] have been recaptured, after the last two, who are part of the [[Islamic Jihad Movement in Palestine|Islamic Jihad Movement]], were arrested in the [[List of cities in Palestine|Palestinian city]] of [[Jenin]] through a joint operation with the [[Yamam]]. [https://timesofindia.indiatimes.com/world/middle-east/last-two-prison-break-fugitives-recaptured-israeli-army/articleshow/86334721.cms (AFP via ''The Times of India'')]
*[[Women's rights in Afghanistan]]
**The new Taliban mayor of [[Kabul]], [[Hamdullah Nomani]], asks women to stay at home in case their job can be filled by a man. Nomani also added that the Taliban "finds it necessary to stop women from working for a while" and instead urged them to work in places where men cannot go due to gender segregation. [https://www.bbc.com/news/world-asia-58614113 (BBC News)]

'''Politics and elections'''
*[[2021 Australian Parliament House sexual misconduct allegations]]
**[[Minister for Industry, Science and Technology|Australian Industry, Science and Technology Minister]] [[Christian Porter]] resigns amid criticism for receiving [[Bribery|anonymous donations]] in his defamation case against the [[Australian Broadcasting Corporation]], who reported on historical rape allegations against him. [https://www.theguardian.com/australia-news/2021/sep/19/christian-porter-takes-appropriate-action-by-quitting-as-minister-scott-morrison-says (''The Guardian'')]
*[[2022 Philippine presidential election]], [[2021 PDP–Laban dispute]]
**A faction of the ruling [[PDP–Laban]] party that is in conflict with incumbent [[President of the Philippines|president]] [[Rodrigo Duterte]] nominates [[Senate of the Philippines|Senator]] [[Manny Pacquiao]] as the party's presidential candidate. [https://www.reuters.com/world/asia-pacific/boxer-manny-pacquiao-nominated-presidential-candidate-philippines-2022-election-2021-09-19/ (Reuters)]
*[[2020–2021 Thai protests]]
**Hundreds of protesters call to "kick out" [[Prime Minister of Thailand|prime minister]] [[Prayuth Chan-ocha]] on the 15th anniversary of the [[2006 Thai coup d'état]], which ousted former prime minister [[Thaksin Shinawatra]]. [https://www.aljazeera.com/news/2021/9/19/protesters-call-to-kick-out-thai-pm-on-coup-anniversary (Al Jazeera)]
